title: Follow the Fluid, Find the Seal

scenes.visual: Title card: Follow the Fluid, Find the Seal.

scenes.tts: The tube's canal is full of fluid. Where is it made, and where does it go?
scenes.visual: The adult brain from the side with the four ventricles glowing blue, colour-matched to chapter 1. A question mark.
scenes.narration: The tube's canal is full of fluid. Where is it made, and where does it go?

scenes.tts: In each ventricle, the choroid plexus secretes cerebrospinal fluid. It is the main source, not the only one.
scenes.visual: Small red fronds in each ventricle release blue droplets. Label: choroid plexus.
scenes.narration: In each ventricle, the choroid plexus secretes cerebrospinal fluid. It is the main source, not the only one.

scenes.tts: The net flow runs one way: from the lateral ventricles to the third, then through the aqueduct into the fourth.
scenes.visual: Arrows run from each lateral ventricle through a small opening into the third ventricle, then through the thin aqueduct into the fourth.
scenes.narration: The net flow runs one way: from the lateral ventricles to the third, then through the aqueduct into the fourth.

scenes.tts: The exit is in the hindbrain. Openings in the fourth ventricle let fluid out around the brain and cord.
scenes.visual: Arrows leave the fourth ventricle through its openings and spread into a blue layer around the brain and spinal cord.
scenes.narration: The exit is in the hindbrain. Openings in the fourth ventricle let fluid out around the brain and cord.

scenes.tts: In most adult humans, the cord's own central canal is largely closed and is not a major route. The fluid circulates around the cord instead.
scenes.visual: A dotted line down the cord's centre fades out while the blue layer around the cord stays. Label: adult human central canal, largely closed.
scenes.narration: In most adult humans, the cord's own central canal is largely closed and is not a major route. The fluid circulates around the cord instead.

scenes.tts: On the usual teaching numbers, the fluid is replaced about three times a day. Is it ever completely fresh?
scenes.visual: A day clock with three loops and a bit around it. Label: about 3.3 turnovers per day.
scenes.narration: On the usual teaching numbers, the fluid is replaced about three times a day. Is it ever completely fresh?

scenes.tts: Picture a glass of dyed water. Pour in clean water slowly, stirring as it overflows.
scenes.visual: A full glass of dark blue water. Clear water pours in from a jug while a spoon stirs; water spills over the rim.
scenes.narration: Picture a glass of dyed water. Pour in clean water slowly, stirring as it overflows.

scenes.tts: After one full glassful, the dye has faded but not gone.
scenes.visual: The colour lightens steadily but stays visibly blue. A gauge counts glassfuls poured: 1.
scenes.narration: After one full glassful, the dye has faded but not gone.

scenes.tts: About thirty-seven percent of the dye is still there. Replacing a volume does not empty it.
scenes.caption: About 37% of the dye is still there. Replacing a volume does not empty it.
scenes.visual: Label beside the glass: about 37% left after one volume. A ghost glass labelled piston would be empty shows the contrast.
scenes.narration: About 37% of the dye is still there. Replacing a volume does not empty it.

scenes.tts: Now plug the cerebral aqueduct while secretion continues. Which ventricles swell?
scenes.visual: A plug drops into the aqueduct. The ventricles wait, unchanged. Question mark.
scenes.narration: Now plug the cerebral aqueduct while secretion continues. Which ventricles swell?

scenes.tts: Everything upstream: both lateral ventricles and the third. Not the fourth, downstream of the plug.
scenes.visual: The lateral and third ventricles balloon; the fourth stays its size. Label: upstream swells.
scenes.narration: Everything upstream: both lateral ventricles and the third. Not the fourth, downstream of the plug.

scenes.tts: Now the seal. In muscle, for example, a protein tracer in the blood leaks out of the capillaries.
scenes.visual: A muscle capillary with dark tracer seeping out into the tissue around it.
scenes.narration: Now the seal. In muscle, for example, a protein tracer in the blood leaks out of the capillaries.

scenes.tts: In the brain's cortex, it goes no farther than the cells lining them.
scenes.visual: A brain capillary beside it: the tracer stays inside. Question: which layer?
scenes.narration: In the brain's cortex, it goes no farther than the cells lining them.

scenes.tts: Three layers could be the seal: the endothelial cells, the basement membrane around them, and astrocyte endfeet outside.
scenes.visual: An electron-micrograph-style capillary cross-section. Three layers highlight in turn: 1 endothelium, 2 basement membrane (a thin band), 3 astrocyte endfeet wrapped around the vessel.
scenes.narration: Three layers could be the seal: the endothelial cells, the basement membrane around them, and astrocyte endfeet outside.

scenes.tts: In nineteen sixty-seven, Thomas Reese and Morris Karnovsky injected horseradish peroxidase into mice. Wherever this enzyme lies, a chemical reaction leaves a dense deposit an electron microscope can see.
scenes.caption: In 1967, Thomas Reese and Morris Karnovsky injected horseradish peroxidase into mice. Wherever this enzyme lies, a chemical reaction leaves a dense deposit an electron microscope can see.
scenes.visual: Card: Reese and Karnovsky, 1967. A syringe adds tracer to a mouse vein; in the tissue, the enzyme turns a reagent into a dark deposit; the electron-micrograph cross-section returns.
scenes.narration: In 1967, Thomas Reese and Morris Karnovsky injected horseradish peroxidase into mice. Wherever this enzyme lies, a chemical reaction leaves a dense deposit an electron microscope can see.

scenes.tts: Which layer stopped the tracer?
scenes.visual: The three labelled layers pulse in turn. Question mark.
scenes.narration: Which layer stopped the tracer?

scenes.tts: The endothelial cells. The deposit filled the vessel and went no farther. That holds for this tracer.
scenes.visual: A dark deposit fills the lumen and stops at the endothelium. Basement membrane and endfeet stay clean.
scenes.narration: The endothelial cells. The deposit filled the vessel and went no farther. That holds for this tracer.

scenes.tts: Tight junctions between those cells were the probable block.
scenes.visual: Zoom to the seam between two endothelial cells; a tight junction glows. Label: probable block.
scenes.narration: Tight junctions between those cells were the probable block.

scenes.tts: Then Milton Brightman and Reese put the tracer into the ventricles instead.
scenes.visual: Card: Brightman and Reese. Tracer is placed in a ventricle instead of the blood.
scenes.narration: Then Milton Brightman and Reese put the tracer into the ventricles instead.

scenes.tts: It spread between brain cells, reached the capillaries from outside, and stopped at the same junctions.
scenes.visual: Dark tracer spreads through the tissue toward the capillary and halts at the endothelial junctions from the outside.
scenes.narration: It spread between brain cells, reached the capillaries from outside, and stopped at the same junctions.

scenes.tts: Two experiments, run in opposite directions, pointed to the same layer.
scenes.visual: Both panels side by side, an arrow from each meeting at the endothelium.
scenes.narration: Two experiments, run in opposite directions, pointed to the same layer.

scenes.tts: A second seal sits on a specialized part of the tube's lining. In the choroid plexus, leaky capillaries lie under a sealed epithelium.
scenes.visual: A choroid plexus frond: tracer leaks from its capillaries but stops at the epithelium above. Label: blood-CSF barrier.
scenes.narration: A second seal sits on a specialized part of the tube's lining. In the choroid plexus, leaky capillaries lie under a sealed epithelium.

scenes.tts: So the net flow runs one way through the tube. Two main seals, both selective, decide what gets in from the blood.
scenes.visual: The whole brain with flow arrows and two highlighted seals. Takeaway card: net one-way flow; two selective seals.
scenes.narration: So the net flow runs one way through the tube. Two main seals, both selective, decide what gets in from the blood.

scenes.visual: End card: Follow the Fluid, Find the Seal.
